query: Can I bill C124 as MRP for a patient discharged after 3 days?
expected_answer_elements: C124 is billable as MRP (Most Responsible Physician)
Patient must be admitted for at least 48 hours
3 days = 72 hours exceeds the 48-hour requirement
C124 is a subsequent visit code used on day of discharge
C124 requires completion of discharge summary, follow-up care arrangement, and discharge medications
Cite: OHIP Schedule of Benefits, General Preamble page 30, Fee Code C124
expert_answer: Yes, C124 can be billed as MRP for a patient discharged after 3 days. The patient must be in hospital for 48 hours to bill C124. Since 3 days (72 hours) exceeds this requirement, C124 is appropriate. C124 is a subsequent visit code used on the day of discharge and requires: (1) completion of the discharge summary, (2) arrangement of follow-up care as necessary, and (3) prescription of discharge medications. Note that C124 is not payable for transfers within the same hospital. (Source: OHIP Schedule of Benefits, General Preamble page 30; verified via dr-bill.ca and JCL Medical Billing)

query: What is the fee for a comprehensive assessment A003?
expected_answer_elements: A003 fee amount is $84.45
A003 is a General Assessment code
Used in family practice and practice in general
Limited to 1 per patient per 12-month period
Less time spent with patient than a consultation (A005)
Cite: OHIP Schedule of Benefits, Section A - Family Practice and Practice in General
expert_answer: The fee for OHIP code A003 (General Assessment) is $84.45. A003 is used for general assessments in family practice and practice in general settings. This code is limited to 1 per patient per 12-month period and typically requires less time spent with the patient compared to a full consultation (A005). The general assessment should include a comprehensive evaluation of the patient's condition appropriate to the presenting complaint. (Source: OHIP Schedule of Benefits, Section A; verified via dr-bill.ca and DoctorCare billing guides)

query: Which discharge codes apply for a Thursday discharge after Monday 2pm admission?

match_criteria.reason: Discharge code eligibility based on timing

expected_answer_elements: Calculate length of stay: Monday 2pm to Thursday (discharge time not specified)
If discharged Thursday before 2pm: less than 48 hours - C124 NOT eligible
C122 can be billed as MRP subsequent visit on day 2 (Tuesday)
C123 can be billed as MRP subsequent visit on day 3 (Wednesday)
C124 requires minimum 48 hours in hospital as MRP
If Thursday discharge is after 2pm: 48+ hours - C124 becomes eligible
Cite: OHIP Schedule of Benefits, General Preamble page 30, MRP discharge codes
expert_answer: For a Thursday discharge after Monday 2pm admission, the applicable discharge codes depend on the exact discharge time on Thursday. Length of stay calculation: Monday 2pm to Thursday 2pm = exactly 48 hours. If the patient is discharged Thursday BEFORE 2pm, they have been in hospital for less than 48 hours, so C124 is NOT eligible. In this case, you can bill: C122 (MRP subsequent visit day 2), C123 (MRP subsequent visit day 3), and a regular subsequent visit on discharge day. If discharged Thursday at 2pm or AFTER, the patient meets the 48-hour requirement and C124 (discharge code) becomes eligible. C124 requires: (1) minimum 48 hours in hospital, (2) completion of discharge summary, (3) arrangement of follow-up care, and (4) prescription of discharge medications. Remember to add E083 (30% MRP premium) to all MRP subsequent visit codes. (Source: OHIP Schedule of Benefits, General Preamble page 30; verified via dr-bill.ca and JCL Medical Billing)

query: Can I bill a consultation in the ER as an internist?

match_criteria.reason: ER consultation billing rules for specialists

expected_answer_elements: Yes, internists can bill consultations in the ER
Must use A-prefix consultation codes (e.g., A135 for internist consultation)
Requires written request from referring physician or nurse practitioner
Can add special visit premiums (K-prefix) for travel and time
Use A-prefix codes, not C-prefix codes, for ER consultations
If admitting as MRP, can add E082 premium (30% of consultation fee)
Cite: OHIP Schedule of Benefits, Consultations section
expert_answer: Yes, as an internist you can bill a consultation in the ER. You must use the A-prefix consultation codes (e.g., A135 for Internal Medicine consultation at $157.00) rather than C-prefix codes. The key requirements are: (1) written request from the referring physician or nurse practitioner, and (2) the consultation meets the standard consultation definition in the Schedule of Benefits. When billing ER consultations, you should use A-prefix codes and can add special visit premiums (K-prefix codes) for travel and time of day. If you are admitting the patient and becoming the Most Responsible Physician (MRP), you can also add the E082 premium (30% of the consultation fee). Do not use C-prefix consultation codes in the ER, as these are for non-emergency inpatient consultations only and special visit premiums do not apply to them. (Source: OHIP Schedule of Benefits, Consultations and Visits section; verified via OMA billing guides and dr-bill.ca)

query: What premiums apply for a house call to an elderly patient?
expected_answer_elements: Travel premiums: B960-B964 ($36.40) depending on time of day
First person seen premiums: B990-B998 ($20.00 to $100.00) depending on time
Additional person seen premiums: B991-B999 if seeing multiple patients
Complex house call code A900 ($45.15) for frail/elderly/housebound patients
Special visit premiums vary by time: weekday daytime, evening, weekend, night
Premiums are billed in addition to the base visit/assessment code
Elderly patient defined as 65+ with complex needs, cognitive impairment, or reduced mobility
Cite: OHIP Schedule of Benefits, Special Visit Premiums section
expert_answer: For a house call to an elderly patient, several premiums apply in addition to the base visit code. First, you can bill A900 (Complex House Call Assessment) at $45.15 if the patient is frail, elderly (65+), or housebound. Elderly patients qualify if they have complex medical management needs, cognitive impairment, age-related reduced mobility, or unexplained functional decline. In addition to A900, you can add: (1) Travel Premium (B960-B964 = $36.40 depending on time of day), and (2) First Person Seen Premium (B990 = $20.00 weekday daytime; B992 = $40.00 with sacrifice of office hours; B994 = $60.00 evenings; B998 = $75.00 weekends/holidays; B996 = $100.00 nights). If seeing multiple patients at the same location, use Additional Person Seen premiums (B991-B999) for subsequent patients. For palliative home visits, use K023 instead of A900 and B966 ($36.40) for the travel premium. All premiums are billed together with the base assessment code on the same claim. (Source: OHIP Schedule of Benefits, Special Visit Premiums; verified via dr-bill.ca, DoctorCare, and OMA billing guides)
